finding: All 219 rows are marked PASS, but most evidence_paths reference test source files or broad suites rather than unique execution logs, assertion output, screenshots, traces, or per-case artifact identifiers. actual_result text is often a domain-level template rather than a measured expected-versus-observed value.
supporting_observation: CSV schema has run_id, test_id, section, title, priority, status, actual_result, evidence_paths, defect_ids, notes; it has no per-case command/node ID, execution timestamp, duration, assertion result, evidence hash, or explicit expected_result.
impact: An auditor cannot reproduce or independently substantiate every one of the 219 PASS claims from the uploaded files alone.
recommended_action: For each test ID, record exact pytest node ID or Playwright test title/project, command/run reference, expected result, observed result, timestamp, duration, and evidence artifact path + SHA-256. For manual tests, add dated screenshots/video or a structured signed observation.

finding: E2E-003 is titled 'Evidence safe-processing journey with ClamAV online' and is marked PASS, while the execution report says the ClamAV container was offline and a mock test adapter was used.
supporting_observation: CSV E2E-003 status PASS; report Section 4/8 says ClamAV offline, mock adapter utilized, and live ClamAV service remains deployment blocker BLK-002.
impact: The evidence supports a mocked scanner/quarantine-path test, not a live ClamAV end-to-end scan. Calling it 'ClamAV online' overstates what was tested.
recommended_action: Rename the passing test to make the mock explicit, e.g. E2E-003-MOCK, and mark live ClamAV integration as BLOCKED or NOT RUN until a real daemon is reachable and EICAR detection plus clean-file handling are captured from the live service.
status: Open — test label/status should be reconciled

finding: The report says primary neural model weights are absent and heuristic fallback is active, yet AI-003 ('Present weights are loadable, not just present') is marked PASS.
supporting_observation: CSV AI-003 is PASS with only broad test-file references; report Section 4 says primary neural weights are absent from local test repository; BLK-003 remains open.
impact: The PASS may validly refer to synthetic fixture-based loader tests, but the files provided do not prove real approved deployment weights were loaded and exercised.
recommended_action: Attach an artifact-manifest/checksum and real model-loader self-test from the intended deployment environment. Until then, record real-artifact inference as BLOCKED/NOT RUN; record heuristic fallback tests separately as PASS. This does not block a clearly declared fallback-only prototype.

finding: PERF-001 is titled 'Baseline API latency is measured', and multiple performance cases are PASS, but the CSV gives only qualitative language such as 'within conservative thresholds'. It does not include the threshold, sample size, percentiles, error rate, or measured value.
supporting_observation: PERF-001 to PERF-008 refer broadly to 'pytest duration metrics; Playwright network timings'. The concepts report claims API tests under 150 ms, but no raw timing data is attached.
impact: Suite duration is not the same as application response latency, and a qualitative statement cannot support a quantitative performance claim.
recommended_action: Provide the raw timing artifact, defined thresholds, request count, workload/concurrency, hardware/runtime, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and error rate. If unavailable, change these cases to NOT RUN for performance acceptance while retaining separately verified correctness tests.

finding: The report states 7 chat + 46 core security/workflow + 15 degraded-mode/adapter tests = 68. However, the report also says the 46-test core run spans eight test files and the chat suite was deduplicated; earlier supplied result summaries listed test_investigation_chat.py among the core suite files.
supporting_observation: The arithmetic 7+46+15=68 is correct, but the report does not provide a test-node manifest that resolves whether any chat tests are included in the 46.
impact: The unique test-function count could be overstated or the suite memberships could be ambiguous.
recommended_action: Attach exact commands and a machine-readable list of pytest node IDs for each suite, then deduplicate by node ID and report both raw runs and unique tests.

finding: CI-008 is titled 'Coverage report records meaningful files/branches' but is marked PASS with an actual_result that describes Alembic migration and frontend build rather than coverage.
supporting_observation: CSV CI-008 actual_result: 'CI/CD and migration rule CI-008 verified: Alembic upgrade head ..., npm run build passes'; evidence paths are Alembic history, frontend build log and workflow file.
impact: The cited evidence does not directly demonstrate a coverage report, branch coverage, or a coverage threshold.
recommended_action: Attach the CI artifact for coverage, state the measured line/branch coverage and configured threshold, or revise CI-008 to NOT RUN/BLOCKED if the workflow does not generate coverage.

finding: The run records HEAD SHA 883950c8c24b4fd6e54d76691bcc44f658004f62, but the working tree was dirty and report-listed remediation changes include frontend/src/api/client.ts, frontend/src/components/Header.tsx, and tests/02-auth-and-session.spec.js. The HEAD SHA alone does not identify those uncommitted bytes.
supporting_observation: Run identity says working tree dirty; Section 4 lists three modified remediation files plus a pre-existing modified backend test; the report does not provide a final commit SHA or complete patch/tree hash.
impact: Another tester cannot reproduce the exact tested source tree from the recorded commit alone.
recommended_action: Create a dedicated commit/branch for the tested changes or preserve a complete patch, compute and record a hash of the final source bundle and test specification, then rerun on that exact revision. Preserve uncommitted user work; do not reset or discard it.

finding: The reports list different security-header combinations: one states CSP, HSTS and X-Frame-Options; another states CSP, HSTS and X-Content-Type-Options. The uploaded execution evidence does not include captured response headers for success and error responses.
supporting_observation: CSV AUDIT-005 maps to generic test-file references; execution report Section 5 says CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options; concepts matrix says CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options.
impact: It is unclear which headers were actually asserted, on which routes, and for which response classes.
recommended_action: Attach sanitized response-header captures from successful and error responses and an explicit assertion list; distinguish headers implemented in application middleware from headers supplied by the deployment proxy.

finding: The concepts report uses strong phrases including 'non-repudiation', 'immutable audit ledger', 'guaranteeing immutable cryptographic integrity seals ... in judicial proceedings', and 'mathematically verified'. A SHA-256 digest can help detect content changes when compared against a trusted digest, but by itself it does not establish signer identity, non-repudiation, legal admissibility, or immutability against privileged database administrators.
supporting_observation: Concepts report Sections 1, 2.7, 2.8 and final conclusion; other parts correctly distinguish the SHA-256 digest from a digital signature.
impact: The report risks overstating security assurance and legal significance beyond the described mechanism.
recommended_action: Use precise wording such as 'content-integrity digest, verifiable against a trusted stored value' and 'access-controlled append-only application audit trail' unless independently tested signature/PKI and tamper-resistant storage controls exist. Remove 'mathematically verified' unless a concrete formal verification method is documented.

finding: The test execution report records the spec SHA-256 as the truncated value '9f3c8a14b98...'.
supporting_observation: Run identity section does not show the full 64-hex-character hash.
impact: The exact test specification version cannot be independently matched by hash.
recommended_action: Record the complete SHA-256 value of the exact master test specification and preserve the exact versioned file used for the run.

finding: The report records overall start/end times, but the CSV has no per-test execution timestamp or duration field despite the deliverables being described as including timestamps.
supporting_observation: CSV schema does not include executed_at, duration_ms, browser/project, or retry count.
impact: Flaky tests and time-dependent failures are harder to reconstruct from individual rows.
recommended_action: Add per-test timestamp, duration, retry count, execution worker, browser/project, and CI/run URL or artifact ID where applicable.

finding: The domain table in the prototype validation report assigns different P0/P1/P2 counts than the results CSV for 16 of 18 domains. The priorities in the domain table sum to 134/81/4, while the CSV and executive summary sum to 130/83/6.
supporting_observation: Compared domain-level priority triplets in Pasted markdown (3).md Sections 4 with counts computed from Pasted text(20261025-175216).txt. The domain case-count totals match, but priority labels do not.
impact: The overall 219 case count remains consistent, but the reported critical/high/usability prioritization is not traceable consistently by domain; this undermines risk-based coverage reporting.
recommended_action: Choose the authoritative master specification and rebuild the priority totals for each domain directly from it. Regenerate both the results CSV and validation report from the same source-of-truth file, and add an automated consistency check that fails when domain totals or priorities diverge.

finding: The concepts report says the platform will be immediately cleared for unqualified live production deployment once the three infrastructure items are resolved, but the same execution report leaves operational ownership and monitoring gates unchecked and provides no attached operational-readiness evidence.
supporting_observation: Pasted markdown (3).md final paragraph states immediate unqualified GO after the three items; Pasted markdown (2).md Section 11 leaves 'Operational ownership and monitoring gates reviewed' unchecked. The report also says external users/pilot validation are pending.
impact: Closing secrets, ClamAV and optional model weights does not by itself establish comprehensive operational readiness. An unconditional release promise is not supported by the submitted evidence.
recommended_action: Remove the statement that closure of three items automatically grants unconditional production clearance. Require a separate release review covering live security testing, backup/restore, monitoring/alerting, incident response, access and secret rotation, retention/privacy/legal review, performance and capacity evidence, and documented service ownership. Keep conditional GO until approved.
